gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Cast-iron lowercase, drawn with one constant stroke. Noto Sans Myanmar follows in a plain sans with a dense, heavy-looking band of text and a broad, welcoming c, which is the pair's strongest pull.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Edo SZ gives you a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, its curves never thinning at the turns. Noto Sans Nabataean reads smoothly, its wide-open s curves standing nearly cap-tall.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Marker-tip letters with a lowercase as tall as cast iron capitals define Edo SZ, which holds one stroke width throughout. And Noto Sans Nag Mundari does the quieter job, its half-unwrapped c and s shapes carrying a plain sans text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu reads tall and modern, its terminals held far from the stroke body. But Edo SZ is what holds the pair together, with round bowls whose walls never swell or taper anywhere.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Classic in feel, Edo SZ cuts its letters like bent wire, with the height of cast iron capitals in its lowercase. Noto Sans Ogham comes in clean and contemporary, its tall bodies looking bold and its e wide open at the gap. Larger text for the heading helps it stand apart.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Cultural and classic, Edo SZ draws crossbars exactly as thick as its stems, with a lowercase that stands like cast iron capitals. And Noto Sans Ol Chiki sets words as solid blocks, its curve tails held well back, so sans-serif text sits quietly under the heading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Edo SZ has no thick-thin swing at all, just a lowercase standing like cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Old Hungarian feels approachable on the page, with large open counters in tall a, e and s that stay clear at tiny sizes.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Cast iron stature, minus the pressure swell at the corners. Edo SZ makes the headline, and Noto Sans Old Italic follows in sans with barely any gap between x-height and cap height, curve endings kept well apart.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and tall, with terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs. And Edo SZ does the showier work, its drafting-pen outlines keeping one constant nib width, while the sans-serif body simply packs in the text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-permi: Edo SZ never swells like brush lettering, holding one stroke width under a lowercase with cast iron stature. And Noto Sans Old Permic matches it with rounded forms open to the side, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals.
